Fake xcrun and maestro for the capture-app, run-parity and setup-parity-sim self-tests. Each fixture folder holds a scenario.json the fakes read from the working directory. The fake xcrun writes each launch's nonce (from the -parity query) to $FAKE_PARITY_STATE, and the fake maestro adds the marker parity.launch.<nonce> to the dump it prints, as the app's parity root does; scenario.omitNonce leaves it out (always), scenario.omitNonceDumps: n leaves it out of the first n dumps of each launch only (capture-app reads the hierarchy again, up to 3 dumps), and scenario.requireArgs (for example --device <udid> --driver-host-port 22187) makes any other call get scenario.otherSession, another simulator's screen without the marker.

fake-clock.mjs pins the wall clock of a script started with node --import <it> to $FAKE_NOW (an ISO instant): the check-signoff --draft local-day case runs at 2026-09-30T23:17:00Z in TZ=Europe/Berlin (01:17 local on 1 October) and expects the date 2026-10-01.
